## Scope

<!-- What does this change do, and what does it deliberately not do? -->

## Test evidence

<!-- Commands run and their totals (pass / fail / skipped), e.g. `npm run verify`, `cargo test`. Say which opt-in tests were run and which were not. -->

## Numerical references

<!-- For engineering calculations: the authoritative source or external tool, its version, how fixtures were generated, and the tolerance with its justification. Write "none" if not applicable. Expected values must not come from the implementation under test. -->

## Security impact

<!-- New inputs, parsers, HTML sinks, storage, network endpoints, native commands or permissions? How is untrusted data handled? -->

## Accessibility impact

<!-- Keyboard access, focus, labels, contrast, reduced motion. -->

## Project schema compatibility

<!-- Does the project format change? Is there a migration and a test for old files? -->

## Hardware claims

<!-- Any claim about physical devices must link to a qualification record made on real hardware. Mocked or simulated runs are not hardware evidence. -->

## Licence and provenance

<!-- New dependencies, fixtures, firmware or assets: version, SPDX licence, source and review. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Capability ledger and documentation match what the code actually does
- [ ] No secrets, credentials or personal data in code, fixtures or logs
- [ ] No test weakened to make it pass
